# Exact aggregate domain for within-pair tetrahedral corrections

This is a proved algebraic parameterization. The positivity of the resulting
correction inequalities is not proved here.

Normalize the diagonal point as x+y+z+w=1, with all coordinates positive.
Put P=x+y, R=1-P, a=xy, b=zw, k=a-b, and

    D=k^2+aR+bP>0.

Conversely a triple (P,a,b) comes from such diagonal points exactly when

    0<P<1,          0<a<=P^2/4,         0<b<=R^2/4.     (1)

Indeed x,y are the positive roots with sum P and product a, and z,w are
those with sum R and product b. The possible within-pair swaps do not
change the cap fraction, scalar moment, or either within-pair correction.

## 1. Centrality requires only four polynomial inequalities

Let δ_i=1-3λ_i. The centroid formulas give

    δ_0=(b-kx)/[(x+z)(x+w)],
    δ_1=(b-ky)/[(y+z)(y+w)],
    δ_2=(a+kz)/[(x+z)(y+z)],
    δ_3=(a+kw)/[(x+w)(y+w)].                           (2)

All denominators are positive. Thus the central condition λ_i<=1/3 for
every i is equivalent, on (1), to

    2b-kP>=0,          b^2-bkP+k^2 a>=0,
    2a+kR>=0,          a^2+akR+k^2 b>=0.               (3)

For the first pair these are the sum and product of b-kx,b-ky; for the
second pair they are the sum and product of a+kz,a+kw. Two real numbers
are both nonnegative exactly when their sum and product are nonnegative.
This proves the equivalence, including zero central deficits.

## 2. Pair sums and products of central deficits

Define

    U=P(b+k^2)-2k(a+b),
    V=b^2-bkP+k^2 a,
    W=R(a+k^2)+2k(a+b),
    Z=a^2+akR+k^2 b.

Then

    δ_0+δ_1=U/D,       δ_0 δ_1=V/D,
    δ_2+δ_3=W/D,       δ_2 δ_3=Z/D,       U+W=D.        (4)

For example the first product follows directly from (2), since the two
denominators multiply to D. For the first sum, use

    D_0+D_1=P-2k,
    x D_1+y D_0=2a-kP,

where D_0=(x+z)(x+w), D_1=(y+z)(y+w). Its numerator is then
b(P-2k)-k(2a-kP)=U. The other pair follows in the same way.

Consequently the negative-coordinate correction, when selected, is

    c_-=(4/3)(D-W+Z)/(2D-3W+4Z).                      (5)

This is simply 4/[12-1/λ_2-1/λ_3] after writing λ_i=(1-δ_i)/3. The
analogous positive-coordinate correction replaces (W,Z) by (U,V).

For c_- the corrected cap fraction has numerator and denominator

    F-c_-s = [b(P-a+b) B-N(bP-aR)]/(D B),
    N=D-W+Z,             B=2D-3W+4Z.                  (6)

Thus, whenever B>0, its lower bound 27/64 is equivalent to

    64[b(P-a+b) B-N(bP-aR)]-27D B>=0.                 (7)

Equation (7) is only a candidate inequality. No sign is inferred here.

## 3. An exact middle-pair condition without square roots

On the central domain, the coordinates λ_2,λ_3 are the middle two of the
four centroid coordinates, allowing ties, if and only if δ_2,δ_3 lie in
the interval between δ_0 and δ_1. The positive-pair quadratic is

    q(t)=t^2-(U/D)t+V/D.

The two real roots of the negative-pair quadratic have sum W/D and product
Z/D. At either such root, reduction of q modulo that quadratic gives

    q(t)=((W-U)/D)t+(V-Z)/D.

Both values q(δ_2),q(δ_3) are nonpositive exactly when their sum is
nonpositive and their product is nonnegative. After clearing positive
powers of D, these are exactly

    (W-U)W+2(V-Z)D <=0,                               (8)
    (W-U)^2 Z+(W-U)(V-Z)W+(V-Z)^2 D >=0.               (9)

Since an upward-opening real quadratic is nonpositive precisely between
its real roots, (8)–(9) prove the claimed equivalence. The degenerate case
δ_0=δ_1 is included: q is a square, so both negative-pair roots must equal
the same value. All tied orderings are therefore covered.

Equations (1), (3), (8), and (9) describe the entire central domain for the
within-negative-middle-pair case using only P,a,b. Together with (6) they
provide an exact lower-degree semialgebraic test. Exchanging the positive
and negative groups gives the within-positive-middle-pair case and
complements the cap fraction.
